cyberbullying on mobile devices is less likely in some countries than in others, is more likely to occur among older children, and is more likely to involve SNS and IM.

the mode of cyber victimization, i.e. cyberbullying online only vs. cyberbullying on SNS and mobile devices, is associated with being older (i.e. older adolescents are more likely than younger adolescents to be cyberbullied on SNS and/or mobile devices), being female, higher levels of sensation seeking, psychological distress, and being upset by the cyberbullying experiences.

the differences between those being cyberbullied online only and those being cyberbulllyed on-the-go and suggests that cyberbullying on SNS and/or IM may be the mechanism by which being cyberbullied is more distressing on-the-go.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cyberbullying on mobile devices is associated with more distressing experiences.
cyberbullying on mobile devices (as opposed to online only) is associated with being more distressed and upset by the experience and with psychological difficulties.
being cyberbullied via SNS or IM on a mobile phone is more distressing than cyberbullying via SNS or instant messaging on the computer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
being cyberbullied by mobile phone is more distressing than being cyberbullied only online.
being bullied on-the-go is more likely to happen to older children, females and to children who use the internet on-the go.
cyberbullying on the mobile phone is a unique experience that is more distressing than cyberbullying via the computer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cyberbullying on SNS and/or IM is associated with more distress than cyberbullying on other platforms.
the mode of cyberbullies' communication with their victims is an important factor in understanding the distress associated with cyberbullying.

cyberbullying on mobile devices is not necessarily a distinct experience from cyberbullying online but rather a specific type of experience that can be more upsetting for some children and young people.
